provenance.kind: Project-authored controlled scientific study, not new experimental measurements.
provenance.scope: Results are conditional on the complete stated model, measurement convention and units.

model: A hypothetical single gas phase obeys exactly Z(P)=1+b*P+c*P^2 on 0<=P<=5 bar. Pressure is entered numerically in bar, so b is per bar and c per bar squared. Both coefficients are unknown. Fit only the two calibration observations; the heldout Z is a check. The ideal-gas limit is Z(0)=1.
thermodynamic_definition: At this fixed temperature, ln(phi(P))=integral_0^P[(Z(p)-1)/p]dp, f=phi*P and mu-mu_ideal=R*T*ln(phi). Use the continuous finite integrand at p=0. A value of Z-1 is not itself ln(phi). The one-observation identification question removes all other pressure observations and any coefficient calibration.
